question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [British Territorial Expansion and Expansionist Treaties]
options: Bombay — Transferred to the British Crown from the Portuguese as part of a royal dowry (1661)
Madras — Granted to the English by the Raja of Chandragiri in 1639 to build Fort St. George
Calcutta — Formed by combining three villages (Sutanuti, Gobindapur, Kalikata) purchased by Job Charnock in 1690
Delhi — Captured by the French under Dupleix in 1740, establishing it as a French protectorate
wrong_fact: Delhi was never captured or made a protectorate by the French under Dupleix. Dupleix's influence was confined to southern India (the Carnatic and Deccan). Delhi was occupied by the British in 1803 after the Battle of Delhi.
explanation: The British acquisition of Bombay, Madras, and Calcutta laid the territorial foundations of the three Presidencies. Bombay was acquired via the marriage treaty of Charles II and Catherine of Braganza. Madras was leased from the local Nayak ruler. Calcutta was developed around Fort William on land obtained from Mughal zamindars. Delhi remained the seat of the declining Mughal Empire.

question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Crucial Naval and Military Engagements]
options: Battle of Swally (1612) — Naval battle off Surat where Thomas Best defeated the Portuguese, gaining Mughal favor
Siege of Arcot (1751) — Robert Clive's defense of Arcot which turned the tide of the Second Carnatic War
Battle of Buxar (1764) — Defeat of the combined native coalition, leading to the Treaty of Allahabad
Battle of Colachel (1741) — British defeat of the Travancore forces, securing Kerala for the British
wrong_fact: The Battle of Colachel (1741) was a decisive victory of the Kingdom of Travancore under King Marthanda Varma over the Dutch East India Company (VOC). It did not involve the British, and it crushed Dutch power in Kerala.
explanation: The Battle of Swally convinced Emperor Jahangir to grant trading rights to the English. The Siege of Arcot established Robert Clive's military reputation. Buxar made the British the de facto rulers of Bengal. Colachel is celebrated as a rare example of an Indian kingdom decisively defeating a European naval power.

question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Mughal Farmans and Commercial Grants]
options: Golden Farman (1632) — Issued by the Sultan of Golconda allowing the Dutch and English free trade for a fixed duty
Farman of 1717 — Issued by Emperor Farrukhsiyar granting the English duty-free trade in Bengal (Dastaks)
Nishan of 1651 — Issued by Prince Shuja permitting the English to trade in Bengal in return for a fixed annual payment
Farman of 1615 — Issued by Akbar granting Sir Thomas Roe exclusive military sovereignty over Goa and Diu
wrong_fact: The Farman was negotiated by Sir Thomas Roe with Emperor Jahangir (not Akbar, who died in 1605) and was issued in 1618 for trade in Surat and other Mughal territories. The Mughals did not own Goa or Diu (which were Portuguese) and could not grant sovereignty over them.
explanation: Sir Thomas Roe arrived at the court of Jahangir in 1615 and secured a farman in 1618 granting trade concessions to the English in the Mughal Empire. The Golden Farman of 1632 was issued by the Sultan of Golconda. Prince Shuja's Nishan of 1651 gave trade privileges in Bengal. Farrukhsiyar's Farman of 1717 was the 'Magna Carta' of the English East India Company.
